engine_rules.name: Label Fourth-Based Chords sus4 Not C2 or add-2
engine_rules.falsifier: Any fourth-based chord labeled C2 or add-2 rather than sus4
engine_rules.anchor: My suggestion for a suitable name for this chord would be: G [sus4]

engine_rules.name: Maintain sus4 Label Across All Inversions
engine_rules.falsifier: An inversion of a fourth-based chord reverts to C2 or add-2 notation
engine_rules.anchor: Of course, this applies to all of the inversions as well

engine_rules.name: Route Through 3-Part Voicings Before 4-Part
engine_rules.falsifier: 4-part voicings presented as foundational before 3-part voicings are established
engine_rules.anchor: 3-part chords are easier to play than 4-part chords

engine_rules.name: Enforce 4-Part as Maximum Voicing Density
engine_rules.falsifier: A chord voicing is constructed with 5 or more simultaneous voices
engine_rules.anchor: leaving out one voice of a 4-part chord

engine_rules.name: Derive 3-Part Chords by Removing Exactly One Voice from 4-Part
engine_rules.falsifier: A 3-part chord is derived by removing more than one voice simultaneously from a 4-part source
engine_rules.anchor: arrive at different 3-part chords by leaving out one voice

engine_rules.name: Each 3-Part Chord Type Appears Exactly Four Times in Derivation Table
engine_rules.falsifier: A 3-part chord type appears fewer or more than 4 times in the voice-omission derivation table
engine_rules.anchor: Each 3-part chord appears four times

engine_rules.name: Catalog 7th(no 3rd) as Independent M-Lode Taxonomy Member
engine_rules.falsifier: 7th(no 3rd) is collapsed into another chord category rather than cataloged as its own distinct type
engine_rules.anchor: we add 3 different 3-part chords: 7th (no 3rd), 7th (no 5th), 3-part Spread Clusters

engine_rules.name: Catalog 7th(no 5th) as Independent M-Lode Taxonomy Member
engine_rules.falsifier: 7th(no 5th) is treated as a reduced or incomplete form of a 4-part chord rather than its own type
engine_rules.anchor: we add 3 different 3-part chords: 7th (no 3rd), 7th (no 5th), 3-part Spread Clusters

engine_rules.name: Catalog 3-Part Spread Clusters as Independent M-Lode Taxonomy Member
engine_rules.falsifier: 3-part Spread Clusters are treated as subordinate to or collapsed into another M-Lode category
engine_rules.anchor: we add 3 different 3-part chords: 7th (no 3rd), 7th (no 5th), 3-part Spread Clusters

engine_rules.name: Expand M-Lode Taxonomy With All Three New 3-Part Chord Types Simultaneously
engine_rules.falsifier: Only one or two of the three new types are added, leaving the M-Lode expansion incomplete
engine_rules.anchor: we add 3 different 3-part chords: 7th (no 3rd), 7th (no 5th), 3-part Spread Clusters

engine_rules.name: Establish GDVL Before Introducing SCVL
engine_rules.falsifier: SCVL is introduced to a student before GDVL is operational as the working mode
engine_rules.anchor: IVLs and FVLs are all examples of SCVL, as opposed to GDVL

engine_rules.name: Classify IVL and FVL as Sub-Types of SCVL
engine_rules.falsifier: IVL or FVL is classified as a type of GDVL or as independent of SCVL
engine_rules.anchor: The IVLs and the FVLs are all examples of SCVL

engine_rules.name: Treat Melodic and Harmonic Domains as Equal Weight
engine_rules.falsifier: Voice-leading decisions systematically favor harmonic motion over melodic motion or vice versa
engine_rules.anchor: excellent voice-leading treats both melody and harmony as equals

engine_rules.name: Diatonic Event Transposition Yields Up to 6 Variants
engine_rules.falsifier: Diatonic transposition of an Event is applied beyond 6 steps without interval-collapse consolidation
engine_rules.anchor: an event can be diatonically transposed to create 6 other events

engine_rules.name: Collapse Intervallically Identical Event Transpositions to One Representative
engine_rules.falsifier: Intervallically identical diatonic event transpositions are listed as separate entries rather than collapsed
engine_rules.anchor: but some of them will be intervallically identical

engine_rules.name: Episode Diatonic Transposition Yields Exactly 6 Modal Variants Without Collapse
engine_rules.falsifier: Episode transposition produces fewer than 6 distinct modal variants or collapses any two modal variants together
engine_rules.anchor: an episode can be diatonically transposed to create 6 other episodes

engine_rules.name: Map Each Transposed Episode to a Distinct Mode
engine_rules.falsifier: Two different episode transpositions are assigned to the same mode
engine_rules.anchor: each corresponds to a different mode

engine_rules.name: Route Events and Episodes Identically Across Melodic, Contrapuntal, and Harmonic Domains
engine_rules.falsifier: An event or episode is restricted to only one domain when the source material permits all three
engine_rules.anchor: Both events and episodes can be melodic, contrapuntal, harmonic

engine_rules.name: Classify Event vs Episode by Note Coverage Not by Length
engine_rules.falsifier: Event/Episode classification is determined solely by duration rather than by note coverage scope
engine_rules.anchor: events as being shorter, while episodes are longer

engine_rules.name: Present Passing-Tone and Embellishment Exercises in C Major First
engine_rules.falsifier: Passing-tone or melodic embellishment exercises on 3-part voicings are initially presented in a key other than C Major
engine_rules.anchor: All of the material that follows in this next section will be presented in C Major (no accidentals)

engine_rules.name: Assign Key Transposition Responsibility to Student After C Major Presentation
engine_rules.falsifier: The system automatically transposes embellishment exercises to other keys without requiring student-driven transposition
engine_rules.anchor: developed the necessary skills to make the needed adjustments

engine_rules.name: Organize Chord Catalog Traversal by Cycle-3 / Cycle-4 Alternation
engine_rules.falsifier: The 840-chord catalog is traversed in a linear or non-alternating root-motion order
engine_rules.anchor: this same approach could be applied to pretty much everything

engine_rules.name: Constrain Catalog to 24 Voicings × 35 Chord Types = 840 Entries
engine_rules.falsifier: The catalog is populated with a number of entries other than 840, or with dimensions other than 24×35
engine_rules.anchor: 3-part chords are easier to play than 4-part chords

engine_rules.name: Sequence 3-Part Catalog Chapters Before 4-Part Catalog Chapters
engine_rules.falsifier: 4-part catalog chapters are presented or indexed before 3-part catalog chapters in the 840 sequence
engine_rules.anchor: 3-part chords are easier to play than 4-part chords

engine_rules.name: Apply M.S.R.P. to Replicate a Melodic Strand Across Voices
engine_rules.falsifier: M.S.R.P. is applied to a non-melodic (purely harmonic) strand
engine_rules.anchor: grip-slipping: more on this later

engine_rules.name: Apply Grip-Slipping to Maintain Fretboard Position Continuity
engine_rules.falsifier: Grip-slipping is applied in a context that forces large positional leaps rather than maintaining continuity
engine_rules.anchor: grip-slipping: more on this later

engine_rules.name: Treat SCVL as the Chromatic Superstructure Over GDVL Diatonic Foundation
engine_rules.falsifier: SCVL is applied without GDVL established as the operating diatonic foundation
engine_rules.anchor: IVLs and FVLs are all examples of SCVL, as opposed to GDVL

engine_rules.name: Assign GDVL as the Voice-Leading Mode for Volumes 1 and 2 Material
engine_rules.falsifier: Volumes 1 or 2 material is classified under SCVL rather than GDVL
engine_rules.anchor: IVLs and FVLs are all examples of SCVL, as opposed to GDVL

engine_rules.name: Apply sus4 Labeling to Both 3-Part and 4-Part Fourth-Based Structures
engine_rules.falsifier: sus4 labeling is applied to 4-part fourth-based structures but not to 3-part, or vice versa
engine_rules.anchor: I will grant you that C2 is shorter, but

engine_rules.name: Derive 7th(no 5th) Exclusively Via Single-Voice Omission from 4-Part 7th Chord
engine_rules.falsifier: 7th(no 5th) is constructed by adding voices rather than by omission from a complete 4-part 7th chord
engine_rules.anchor: arrive at different 3-part chords by leaving out one voice

engine_rules.name: Expose All Four Omission Positions to Reveal Symmetric Derivation Structure
engine_rules.falsifier: Fewer than all four voice-omission positions are explored, leaving the symmetric structure incomplete
engine_rules.anchor: Each 3-part chord appears four times

engine_rules.name: Account for All Seven Modes in Complete Episode Transposition Set
engine_rules.falsifier: A complete episode transposition set contains fewer or more than 7 modal forms
engine_rules.anchor: each corresponds to a different mode

engine_rules.name: Allow Events and Episodes to Span Combined Domains Simultaneously
engine_rules.falsifier: A combined-domain event or episode is split into separate single-domain units
engine_rules.anchor: or in any combination

engine_rules.name: Apply Cycle-3 / Cycle-4 Alternation Principle to Any New Material Beyond the Core Catalog
engine_rules.falsifier: Extended material beyond the 840-chord catalog is organized by a non-cycle-based traversal order
engine_rules.anchor: this same approach could be applied to pretty much everything

engine_rules.name: Reject Any Voicing Construction That Exceeds Four Simultaneous Voices
engine_rules.falsifier: A chord voicing with 5 or more voices passes validation within this system
engine_rules.anchor: leaving out one voice of a 4-part chord

engine_rules.name: Catalog Spread Clusters as Coordinate With Not Subordinate to Other M-Lode Types
engine_rules.falsifier: 3-part Spread Clusters are nested inside or subordinated to 7th(no 3rd) or 7th(no 5th) in the taxonomy
engine_rules.anchor: we add 3 different 3-part chords: 7th (no 3rd), 7th (no 5th), 3-part Spread Clusters

engine_rules.name: Sequence Passing-Tone Learning as C Major Mastery Then Independent Transposition
engine_rules.falsifier: Passing-tone exercises begin in a key with accidentals before C Major is mastered
engine_rules.anchor: All of the material that follows in this next section will be presented in C Major (no accidentals)

engine_rules.name: Define IVL Voice Motion by Interval Relationships Between Voices
engine_rules.falsifier: IVL voice motion is defined by functional harmonic role rather than interval distance
engine_rules.anchor: The IVLs and the FVLs are all examples of SCVL

engine_rules.name: Define FVL Voice Motion by Harmonic Function
engine_rules.falsifier: FVL voice motion is defined by pure interval distance rather than harmonic function
engine_rules.anchor: The IVLs and the FVLs are all examples of SCVL
